newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan caretaker premier rules out martial law.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan caretaker premier rules out martial law.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid on Saturday ruled out the possibility of martial law and said his administration would stick to holding national elections on February 3.

The official APP news agency also quoted him as denying he had developed differences with President Farooq Leghari, who gave him the caretaker job on November 5 after sacking prime minister Benazir Bhutto for alleged maladministration.

"There is no chance for martial law in the country," Khalid told reporters at the Punjab province town of Multan, apparently denying rumours of a possible military takeover sparked by Bhutto's demand that Leghari must step down for a free decision on her court challenge to her dismissal and free elections.
He said his government would not hold a referendum to seek an extension in its mandatory 90-day tenure and "the elections would be held on Feb 3".
Khalid said he was enjoying good relations with Leghari "so there is no question of having any dispute with him".
He also denied speculation in local newspaper reports of his possible resignation calling them "totally fabricated".

Bhutto, who denies charges of corruption and misrule cited as reasons for the dismissal of her three-year-old government, has gone to the Supreme Court with a petition seeking her restoration as prime minister.

"We are demanding the resignation of the president as we believe just, fair and transparent elections are not possible in his presence," APP quoted Bhutto as telling reporters on Friday during a visit to her home district of Larkana in the southern province of Sindh.

She also accuses Leghari and the caretaker cabinet of seeking to keep her Pakistan People's Party out of power and amending an electoral law to benefit her political opponents. The government denies the charge.
